examples.en: The calculator computes numbers quickly.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터는 복잡한 식도 몇 초 만에 연산했어요.
examples.en: The computer calculated even complex formulas in a few seconds.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램이 데이터를 연산하는 데 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time for this program to process the data.

examples.ko: 오늘 수학 시간에 연산할 문제가 많아요.
examples.en: There are a lot of problems to calculate in math class today.

examples.ko: 서버가 값을 연산하고 결과를 화면에 보여 줘요.
examples.en: The server computes the value and shows the result on the screen.

examples.ko: 한 번에 연산해서 답을 내는 방법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a way to work out the answer in one go.

explain: 일상에서 계산할 때는 '계산하다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '연산하다'는 컴퓨터나 수학처럼 식과 값을 처리하는 장면에서 써요. 가게에서 돈을 낼 때는 '계산하다'만 가능해요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '계산하다' far more often. 연산하다 fits computers and math, where formulas and values are processed. When paying at a shop, only '계산하다' works.

examples.en: I completed all the required courses at university.
If you complete this course, you get a certificate.
To graduate, you have to earn forty credits.

examples.ko: 교육을 이수한 사람만 시험을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who have completed the training can take the exam.

examples.ko: 한 학기에 최대 스무 학점까지 이수할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take up to twenty credits in one semester.
I completed the lectures online and received a confirmation letter.

explain: '과목, 과정, 학점, 교육'처럼 정해진 공부를 목적어로 받아요. 아무 일이나 끝낼 때 쓰는 '끝내다'와는 달라요. 학교에서는 '필수 이수', '이수 학점'이라는 말을 많이 봐요.
explain_en: It takes objects like courses, credits, or training, meaning you finish a set program of study. Unlike '끝내다', it is not for finishing just anything. At school you will often see '필수 이수' and '이수 학점'.

examples.en: I sort the files by name.

examples.ko: 엑셀 표를 점수가 높은 순으로 정렬했어요.
examples.en: I sorted the Excel table from the highest score.

examples.ko: 목록을 날짜순으로 정렬하려면 이 버튼을 누르세요.
examples.en: Press this button to sort the list by date.
If you sort them, it is much easier to compare.
I learned how to center-align the text.

examples.ko: 가격이 낮은 순으로 정렬할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can sort from the lowest price.

explain: 엑셀이나 앱에서 '이름순 정렬', '가격순 정렬'처럼 자주 보여요. 글자를 '왼쪽 정렬', '가운데 정렬'로 맞출 때도 써요. 사람을 줄 세울 때는 '줄을 세우다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: You see it often in spreadsheets and apps, as in '이름순 정렬' and '가격순 정렬'. It is also used for text alignment, such as '왼쪽 정렬' or '가운데 정렬'. For lining people up, '줄을 세우다' sounds more natural.

en: look up; check (records); make an inquiry

examples.en: I check my account balance in the app.

examples.ko: 주문 내역을 조회해서 배송 상태를 확인했어요.
examples.en: I looked up my order history and checked the delivery status.

examples.ko: 번호를 입력하면 정보를 조회할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you enter the number, you can look up the information.

examples.ko: 조회하는 데 시간이 오래 걸려서 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The lookup took a long time, so I waited.
I checked my grades on the school website.
Even if you do not check yourself, it comes as a notification.

explain: 은행, 인터넷, 관공서에서 이미 있는 기록을 찾아볼 때 써요. '검색하다'는 넓은 인터넷에서 찾는 것이고, '조회하다'는 내 정보나 정해진 자료를 확인하는 느낌이에요. '잔액 조회', '주문 조회'처럼 메뉴 이름으로 많이 봐요.
explain_en: Used for looking up existing records at banks, websites, and public offices. '검색하다' is searching the wide internet, while 조회하다 is checking your own data or a fixed set of records. It often appears as menu names like '잔액 조회' and '주문 조회'.

examples.en: The commander gave orders to the soldiers.
The main character of that movie is a brave commander.

examples.ko: 새 지휘관은 다음 주에 부대에 와요.
examples.en: The new commander arrives at the unit next week.

examples.ko: 지휘관의 말에 모두가 조용히 귀를 기울였어요.
examples.en: Everyone listened quietly to the commander's words.
My uncle worked as a commander in the army.
You have to report the situation to the commander right away.

explain: 회사나 팀의 리더에게는 쓰지 않아요. 군대, 경찰, 소방처럼 명령으로 움직이는 조직의 책임자일 때 써요. 오케스트라를 이끄는 사람은 '지휘자'예요.
explain_en: It is not used for the leader of a company or team. It fits heads of organizations that run on orders, such as the military, police, or fire service. The person leading an orchestra is a '지휘자'.

examples.en: This book covers the whole of Korean history.

examples.ko: 이 보험은 다양한 사고를 포괄하고 있어요.
examples.en: This insurance covers a wide range of accidents.

examples.ko: 두 가지 의견을 포괄하는 방법을 찾아봐요.
examples.en: Let's find a way to include both opinions.
We surveyed across all age groups.

examples.ko: 모든 경우를 포괄할 수 있는 말을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a word that can cover every case.

examples.ko: 계약서가 여러 경우를 포괄했는지 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check whether the contract covers the various cases.

explain: '포함하다'는 일부로 들어 있다는 느낌이고, '포괄하다'는 넓은 범위를 한꺼번에 감싼다는 느낌이에요. 책, 보험, 정책, 법처럼 범위가 큰 대상에 어울려요. '포괄적'이라는 모양으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '포함하다' feels like something is included as one part, while 포괄하다 feels like wrapping a wide range all at once. It suits big-scope subjects such as books, insurance, policies, and laws. It is also very common as '포괄적' (comprehensive).

examples.en: Everyone marveled at the beautiful scenery.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 노래 실력에 저절로 감탄해요.
examples.en: I can't help marveling at that singer's skill.

examples.ko: 사람들은 그의 그림을 보고 감탄하며 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: People saw his painting and applauded in admiration.
It was food so delicious it made me marvel.
The teacher marveled at the student's fast progress.
Sounds of admiration could be heard here and there.

explain: 보통 '~에 감탄하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 대단하고 멋져서 저절로 소리가 나올 때 쓰고, 마음이 움직이는 '감동하다'와는 조금 달라요. 감탄하는 소리는 '와!' 같은 '감탄사'로 나와요.
explain_en: It is usually used with the particle '에', as in '~에 감탄하다'. Use it when something is so impressive that you react spontaneously. It differs a little from '감동하다', being emotionally moved. The sound itself comes out as an interjection like '와!' (a '감탄사').

examples.ko: 옛날에 그 나라에는 현명한 군주가 있었어요.
examples.en: Long ago, that country had a wise monarch.

examples.ko: 군주는 신하들의 말을 잘 들어야 해요.
examples.en: A monarch has to listen well to his subjects.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 조선의 군주들에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned about the monarchs of Joseon.

examples.ko: 백성을 아끼기로 유명한 군주를 책에서 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read in a book about a monarch famous for caring for his people.

examples.ko: 군주의 결정에 나라의 운명이 달려 있었어요.
examples.en: The fate of the country depended on the monarch's decision.

examples.ko: 소설에는 잔인한 군주와 용감한 기사가 나와요.
examples.en: In the novel, a cruel monarch and a brave knight appear.

explain: '왕'은 평소에도 쓰고, '군주'는 역사나 책에서 주로 만나요. 왕, 황제, 여왕을 한꺼번에 묶어 말할 때 편해요. 지금도 왕이 있는 나라를 '군주제 국가'라고 불러요.
explain_en: '왕' (king) is used in everyday talk, while 군주 shows up mostly in history and books. It is handy for grouping kings, emperors, and queens together. A country that still has a king is called a '군주제 국가' (monarchy).

examples.en: The character motions in this game look natural.

examples.ko: 영상 편집에서 모션을 넣으면 더 멋져 보여요.
examples.en: If you add motion in video editing, it looks cooler.
You need to practice the hand motions together too.

examples.ko: 슬로 모션으로 다시 보니 장면이 잘 보여요.
examples.en: Watching again in slow motion, I can see the scene well.
Sound plays to match the motion.
They make movies using motion capture technology.

explain: 영어 motion에서 온 말이고, 영상, 게임, 디자인에서 '움직임, 동작'의 느낌으로 써요. 일상에서 몸의 움직임은 '동작'이라고 해요. '슬로 모션', '모션 캡처'처럼 묶음으로 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Borrowed from English 'motion', used in video, games, and design for movement. For ordinary body movement, Koreans say '동작'. It often appears in fixed sets like '슬로 모션' and '모션 캡처'.

examples.en: The cup fell on the floor and smashed.
My phone screen is smashed.

examples.ko: 커피잔이 박살 나는 소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by the sound of the coffee cup smashing.
My dream was shattered, and I had a hard time for a while.

examples.ko: 박살 난 유리 조각을 조심해서 치웠어요.
examples.en: I carefully cleaned up the pieces of smashed glass.

examples.ko: 계획이 박살 날 뻔했지만 친구가 도와줬어요.
examples.en: The plan almost fell apart, but my friend helped.

explain: '박살이 나다'는 물건이 산산이 부서질 때, '박살 내다'는 부수거나 크게 이길 때 써요. 말투가 거칠어서 뉴스나 격식 있는 글에서는 '파손되다', '크게 이기다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 상대 팀을 박살 냈어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 부술 때뿐 아니라 시합에서 크게 이길 때도 써요. 말투가 거칠어서 친한 사이에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only for breaking objects but also for winning a game by a big margin. The tone is rough, so it suits close friends.

explain_en: '박살이 나다' is for things breaking into pieces, and '박살 내다' is for smashing something or winning big. The tone is rough, so news and formal writing use words like '파손되다' or '크게 이기다' instead.

examples.en: I arrange the books in order of height.
The students arranged the chairs in a circle.
I did homework arranging words in alphabetical order.

examples.ko: 사진을 시간 순서로 배열해서 앨범을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I arranged the photos in time order and made an album.
If you arrange the letters properly, it becomes a sentence.
I arranged the flowers by color and took a picture.

explain: '정리하다'는 깔끔하게 치우는 느낌이고, '배열하다'는 순서나 모양을 정해서 늘어놓는 느낌이에요. '정렬하다'와 뜻이 가까운데, 컴퓨터나 표에서 순서대로 맞출 때는 '정렬'을 더 많이 봐요. 단어를 순서에 맞게 놓는 문제에도 써요.
explain_en: '정리하다' feels like tidying up, while '배열하다' feels like setting things out in a chosen order or shape. It is close to '정렬하다', but for putting data or tables in order, '정렬' is the more common word. It also appears in tasks of putting words in the right order.

examples.en: I made up for the weak parts and submitted it again.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 단점을 계속 보완하고 있어요.
examples.en: This app keeps improving on its weaknesses.
I practice every day to make up for my weakness.
Please submit after you supplement the plan.

examples.ko: 보안 문제를 빨리 보완해야 한다는 의견이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Some said the security problem must be fixed quickly.
We work while covering each other's weak points.

explain: '부족한 점, 약점, 단점'을 목적어로 자주 받아요. 잘못된 것을 바로잡는 '고치다'와 달리, 있는 것에 모자란 부분을 채운다는 느낌이에요. 발음이 비슷한 '보안'(안전 지키기)과 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It often takes objects like shortcomings, weaknesses, or flaws. Unlike '고치다', which corrects something wrong, it feels like filling in what is lacking. Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding '보안' (security).

examples.en: Obtaining the information was harder than I thought.
They say the source is a secret.
I lined up from morning to get a ticket.

examples.ko: 새 소식을 입수하는 대로 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll tell you as soon as I get new information.
We obtained that material yesterday.
A photo obtained by the police appeared in the news.

explain: '정보, 자료, 증거'처럼 쉽게 구하기 어려운 것에 써요. 가게에서 물건을 사는 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스에서 '입수했다'는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: Used for hard-to-get things like information, materials, or evidence. It is not used for buying goods at a shop. You often hear '입수했다' (obtained) in the news.

examples.en: War veterans gathered at the memorial ceremony.
That country could not decide to enter the war.
Because of the war, many young men left their hometowns.
Opinions about joining the war differ.
When the war participation became known, people worried.

examples.ko: 참전의 기억은 평생 잊을 수 없대요.
examples.en: They say you can never forget the memory of fighting in a war.

explain: 전쟁에 직접 나가 싸운다는 점이 중요해요. 대회나 행사에 나가는 '참가'와 달라서 전쟁 이야기에만 써요. '참전 용사'처럼 굳은 말로 가장 많이 나와요.
explain_en: The key point is going out to fight in a war yourself. Unlike '참가' (joining an event), it is only used for war. It appears most in the fixed phrase '참전 용사' (war veteran).

examples.en: He took part in the war at nineteen.
Before going to war, he left a letter to his family.
Our country was also asked to join the war.
It is a day to honor the soldiers who fought in the war.
It is a story of people who went abroad and fought in the war.
They say he agonized for a long time over whether to join the war.

explain: '전쟁에 참전하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 일반 대회나 행사에는 '참가하다', '참여하다'를 써요. 이미 전쟁이라는 뜻이 들어 있어서 '전쟁에'를 빼도 말이 통해요.
explain_en: Used with the particle '에', as in '전쟁에 참전하다'. For ordinary contests or events, use '참가하다' or '참여하다'. Since the idea of war is already inside the word, it still works even if you drop '전쟁에'.

examples.en: In the old days, foreign enemies often invaded our country.

examples.ko: 적이 침략해 오자 사람들은 성으로 피했어요.
examples.en: When the enemy invaded, people took refuge in the castle.
In the movie, aliens invade Earth.

examples.ko: 다른 나라를 침략하는 것은 국제법 위반이에요.
examples.en: Invading another country violates international law.
It came out that they had made plans to invade.
That region was invaded several times.

explain: 다른 나라를 힘으로 공격해 들어가는 나쁜 일에 써요. 남의 집이나 건물에 몰래 들어가는 것은 '침입하다'예요. 공격을 받은 쪽은 '침략을 당하다', '침략당하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It describes attacking and entering another country by force, so it carries a negative tone. Sneaking into someone's house or building is '침입하다'. The side that gets attacked says '침략을 당하다' or '침략당하다'.

examples.en: A large ship sank in the sea.
The fishing boat almost sank because of the storm.

examples.ko: 영화 속 배는 빙산에 부딪혀 침몰해요.
examples.en: The ship in the movie hits an iceberg and sinks.

examples.ko: 배가 침몰하기 전에 승객들이 모두 내렸어요.
examples.en: All the passengers got off before the ship sank.

examples.ko: 침몰한 배를 찾는 작업이 계속되고 있어요.
examples.en: The work of searching for the sunken ship is continuing.

examples.ko: 오래전에 침몰하고 있던 배를 구한 이야기예요.
examples.en: It is a story about saving a ship that had been sinking long ago.

explain: 주로 배가 물에 가라앉는 사고에 써요. '가라앉다'보다 크고 심각한 사고 느낌이에요. 비유로 '회사가 침몰하다'처럼 크게 무너질 때도 써요.
explain_en: Mostly used when a ship goes under the water in an accident. It feels bigger and more serious than '가라앉다'. It is also used figuratively, as in '회사가 침몰하다', when something collapses badly.

examples.en: There is a button at the bottom of the screen.
Please check the address at the bottom of the page.
Tap the bottom menu and go to settings.
Leave the bottom of the table blank.
If you scroll down, it moves to the bottom.
The colors at the bottom and top of the poster differ.

explain: 반대말은 '상단'이에요. 위치를 말할 때 '아래쪽'보다 딱딱해서 화면, 문서, 표, 안내문에 많이 써요. 대화에서는 '아래'나 '밑'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '상단' (top). It is stiffer than '아래쪽', so you see it on screens, documents, tables, and notices. In conversation, '아래' or '밑' sounds more natural.

examples.en: They say Jumong founded Goguryeo.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 백 년 전에 건국했어요.
examples.en: That country was founded a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 나라를 건국한 왕의 이야기가 드라마로 나왔어요.
examples.en: A drama came out about the king who founded the country.
People who wanted to found a new country gathered.
Many things happened in the process of founding the country.
It is a country that was founded and has continued until now.

explain: 나라를 처음 세울 때만 쓰고, 회사나 학교를 세울 때는 '설립하다', '세우다'를 써요. 주어는 보통 사람이나 왕이에요. 나라가 주어일 때는 '건국되다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is only for founding a country; for companies or schools, use '설립하다' or '세우다'. The subject is usually a person or a king. When the country is the subject, '건국되다' is more common.

examples.en: The bodyguard protects the president.

examples.ko: 가수를 경호하는 사람들이 앞에 서 있어요.
examples.en: The people guarding the singer are standing in front.
They guarded a famous guest at the event hall.
I get nervous when guarding an important guest.

examples.ko: 친구는 경호 회사에서 일하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My friend wants to work at a security company.
The person who had been guarding suddenly ran out.

explain: 위험에서 지키려고 곁에서 사람을 보호할 때 써요. 대상은 대통령, 연예인, 중요한 손님이에요. '지키다'는 집이나 약속에도 쓰지만 '경호하다'는 사람에게만 써요. 그 일을 하는 사람은 '경호원'이에요.
explain_en: Used for staying beside a person to protect them from danger, such as a president, a celebrity, or an important guest. '지키다' also works for houses or promises, but 경호하다 is only for people. The person who does this job is a '경호원'.

examples.en: We climbed the mountain in extreme cold.
The athlete pushed his body to the limit.
My patience reached its limit.
He acted calmly even in an extreme situation.
It was a challenge that went beyond the limit.
He crossed the desert fighting against the extremes.

explain: '한계'는 넘기 어려운 선이고, '극한'은 그 선에 거의 닿은 가장 심한 상태예요. '극한의 추위', '극한 직업'처럼 어려움이 아주 클 때 붙여요. 수학에서는 다른 뜻의 용어로도 나와요.
explain_en: '한계' is a line that is hard to cross, while 극한 is the most severe state, almost at that line. It is attached as in '극한의 추위' (extreme cold) or '극한 직업' (an extremely tough job). In math it is also a term with a different meaning.

examples.en: Dinosaurs went extinct a very long time ago.

examples.ko: 많은 동물이 멸종할 위기에 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Many animals are at risk of going extinct.
When the environment changes, some living things go extinct.
We are protecting tigers so they do not go extinct.
The bones of an extinct animal are in the museum.

examples.ko: 왜 매머드가 멸종했는지 궁금해서 책을 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I was curious why mammoths died out, so I looked in a book.

explain: 주어는 동물이나 식물 같은 생물 종류예요. 사람 한 명이 죽는 일에는 쓰지 않아요. '멸종 위기', '멸종 위기종'처럼 환경 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: The subject is a kind of living thing, such as an animal or plant species. It is not used for one person dying. It appears often in environmental news, as in '멸종 위기' and '멸종 위기종' (endangered species).

examples.en: Our team turned the game around at the end.
They came from behind with a last goal, and everyone was surprised.
There is still a chance to turn things around.

examples.ko: 지던 팀이 갑자기 역전하자 관중이 환호했어요.
examples.en: When the losing team suddenly turned it around, the crowd cheered.
I like stories where someone is losing and then turns it around.

examples.ko: 그가 역전한 뒤로 팀 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After he turned the game around, the team's mood improved.

explain: 스포츠에서 지던 팀이 이기게 될 때 가장 많이 써요. '상황이 역전되다'처럼 피동으로도 자주 말해요. 그렇게 이긴 경기는 '역전승'이에요. '역전'에는 '역 앞'이라는 다른 말도 있어요.
explain_en: Most common in sports when a losing team ends up winning. It is also often said in the passive, as in '상황이 역전되다'. A game won that way is a '역전승'. Note that '역전' can also mean the area in front of a station (역 앞), which is a different word.

examples.en: That player is an idol to children.
Many fans follow the singer like an idol.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 우상이었던 배우를 직접 만났어요.
examples.en: I met in person the actor who was my idol as a child.
Making an idol and worshipping it is dangerous.
My idol is someone who always makes an effort.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 도시 사람들의 우상으로 불려요.
examples.en: That team is called the idol of the city's people.

explain: 존경하고 열광하며 따르는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 닮고 싶은 사람은 '롤모델'이라고 하고, '우상'은 더 열광하는 느낌이에요. 종교에서 섬기는 조각상도 '우상'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Used for a person you admire and follow with great enthusiasm. A person you want to be like is a '롤모델', while 우상 feels more passionate. In religion, a worshipped statue is also called 우상.

examples.ko: 공사 중이라 다른 길로 우회해야 해요.
examples.en: The road is under construction, so we have to detour.
The bus bypassed the accident site.

examples.ko: 막힌 길을 우회하는 방법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to get around the blocked road.

examples.ko: 돌아서 우회하면 십 분 더 걸려요.
examples.en: If you take the detour, it takes ten more minutes.

examples.ko: 우회하지 않고 곧장 가는 길이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a way to go straight without a detour.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 막히는 구간을 우회해서 안내해요.
examples.en: This app guides you around congested sections.

explain: 평소에는 '돌아가다'를 쓰고, '우회하다'는 길 안내나 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 길뿐 아니라 '규제를 우회하다'처럼 부딪치지 않고 피해 가는 일에도 써요. 돌아가는 길은 '우회로'예요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '돌아가다'; 우회하다 is common in navigation and the news. It is used not only for roads but also for avoiding something head-on, as in '규제를 우회하다'. The detour road itself is an '우회로'.

examples.en: Looking at a 3D picture, it feels real.
If you think in a multi-dimensional way, the problem gets easier.
A pop-up card came as a gift.
It is a photo with a strong sense of depth.
This building is known for its three-dimensional design.
That novel is fun because the characters have depth.

explain: '평면'의 반대말이에요. 눈에 보이는 물건뿐 아니라 '입체적인 인물'처럼 여러 면이 있는 사람이나 설명을 칭찬할 때도 써요. 영상이나 게임에서는 '3D'라는 말이 더 많이 들려요.
explain_en: The opposite of '평면' (flat). Besides visible objects, it praises people or explanations that have many sides, as in '입체적인 인물'. In videos and games, you hear '3D' more often.

examples.en: A fighter jet flew fast across the sky.

examples.ko: 공항 근처에서 전투기 소리가 크게 났어요.
examples.en: A loud fighter jet sound came from near the airport.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감 전투기를 손에 들고 놀아요.
examples.en: The child plays holding a toy fighter jet.
A fighter jet's speed is faster than sound.
Fighter jets and passenger planes differ a lot in size.
The air force protects the sky with fighter jets.

explain: '비행기'는 모든 비행기를 가리키고, '전투기'는 싸우는 임무를 가진 군용기예요. 사람을 태우는 비행기는 '여객기', 짐을 싣는 비행기는 '화물기'라고 해요.
explain_en: '비행기' covers all airplanes, while 전투기 is a military aircraft with a combat mission. A plane carrying people is a '여객기', and one carrying freight is a '화물기'.

examples.en: The company raised the funds it needed from a bank.

examples.ko: 행사에 쓸 물건을 직접 조달해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to procure the items for the event ourselves.

examples.ko: 돈을 조달하는 방법을 같이 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's think together about how to raise the money.
I got the ingredients in a hurry and barely made it.
It is not easy to supply the necessary workforce.
I'm worried because there is nowhere to raise the construction costs.

explain: 돈, 재료, 사람처럼 일에 필요한 것을 구해서 대 줄 때 써요. 개인이 물건을 살 때는 '사다', '구하다'라고 하고, '조달하다'는 회사나 단체의 일에 어울려요. '자금 조달', '물자 조달'이 자주 나오는 짝이에요.
explain_en: Used when you obtain and supply what a job needs, such as money, materials, or people. Individuals buying things say '사다' or '구하다', while 조달하다 suits the work of companies and groups. '자금 조달' and '물자 조달' are common pairings.

examples.en: My aim was accurate, so I hit it in one go.
When shooting a bow, I focus on aiming.
I practiced aiming every day.
I aimed wrong, so the arrow missed.

examples.ko: 조준은 끝났고 이제 쏘기만 하면 돼요.
examples.en: The aiming is done, and now I just have to shoot.

examples.ko: 조준의 정확도를 높이는 연습 게임이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a practice game that improves aiming accuracy.

explain: '조준을 하다', '조준이 정확하다'처럼 활, 물총, 게임에서 자주 들려요. 일상에서는 '겨냥'이라는 말도 비슷하게 쓰여요. '목표를 조준하다'처럼 비유로 노리는 대상을 정할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Heard in archery, water guns, and games, as in '조준을 하다' and '조준이 정확하다'. The similar word '겨냥' is also used in daily life. It also works figuratively for picking a target, as in '목표를 조준하다'.

examples.en: The athlete aims at the target.
I aimed the water gun at my friend.

examples.ko: 먼저 조준하고 숨을 멈춘 뒤에 쏘세요.
examples.en: Aim first, hold your breath, and then shoot.
I aimed slowly and shot the arrow.
When aiming, I close one eye.
The gaze aiming at the target is sharp.

explain: '과녁을 조준하다'처럼 대상을 '을/를'로 받아요. 일상에서는 '겨냥하다'도 자주 쓰고, 비유로 '시장을 겨냥하다'라고 하면 '조준하다'보다 더 자연스러워요. 총, 활, 물총을 쏘기 직전의 동작이에요.
explain_en: It takes its target with the object particle, as in '과녁을 조준하다'. In daily speech '겨냥하다' is also common, and figuratively '시장을 겨냥하다' sounds more natural than 조준하다. It is the action right before shooting a gun, bow, or water gun.

examples.ko: 추리 소설을 읽으면 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: Time flies when I read a mystery novel.
The detective began reasoning from a small clue.
His deduction was accurate, so everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 추리의 재미는 범인을 맞히는 데 있어요.
examples.en: The fun of a mystery is in guessing the culprit.
There were few clues, so the deduction had limits.
This game needs deduction and a way with words.

explain: '추리 소설', '추리 영화'처럼 이야기 장르 이름으로 가장 자주 나와요. '추론'은 논리나 공부에서 쓰는 말이고, '추리'는 사건과 범인처럼 단서를 모아 짐작할 때 어울려요. 단서 없이 막연히 하는 것은 '짐작'이에요.
explain_en: Most often seen as a story genre, as in '추리 소설' and '추리 영화'. '추론' is used in logic and academics, while 추리 fits gathering clues about a case or culprit. Guessing with no clues is '짐작'.

examples.en: Look at the clues and try to deduce the culprit.
The detective stayed up all night reasoning out the case.
I worked out the story just from the picture.

examples.ko: 추리할 수 있는 단서가 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: There is not a single clue to reason from.
If you reason through the situation, the answer will appear.

examples.ko: 말투를 보고 기분을 추리하는 건 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to figure out someone's mood from their tone.

explain: 단서를 모아 결론을 이끌어 낼 때 써요. 그냥 '맞혀 보다'와 달리 근거를 따져 본다는 느낌이에요. '~을/를 추리하다'로 쓰고, 명사 '추리'는 '추리 소설'에서 자주 만나요.
explain_en: Used when you gather clues and draw a conclusion. Unlike simply guessing ('맞혀 보다'), it feels like weighing evidence. It takes an object ('~을/를 추리하다'), and the noun 추리 is often met in '추리 소설'.
